narrative.intro: Research Triangle Institute obligated $250M in FY2026 to date across 289 awards, with an average award size of $866K. Obligations were down 30.8% year over year. Fiscal-year obligations peaked at $663M in FY24 and then fell to $362M in FY25 before reaching $250M in FY26. The Department of Health and Human Services is the dominant buyer, accounting for $194M of FY2026 to date obligations. Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services is the largest NAICS market at $91.5M, followed by All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services at $68.6M. Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities, Other Accounting Services, and Computing Infrastructure Providers round out the top markets, with values of $27.4M, $19.5M, and $12.2M respectively. Current-year totals are partial and reflect fiscal year to date activity rather than a full-year picture.

sections.heading: Who are Research Triangle Institute's biggest federal customers?
sections.body: The Department of Health and Human Services obligated $194M to Research Triangle Institute in FY2026 to date. The Environmental Protection Agency and the Department of Labor follow, with $15.7M and $12.9M respectively. The Agency for International Development and the Department of Education also appear in the top buyers with $12.3M and $8.4M.

sections.heading: What does Research Triangle Institute sell to the government?
sections.body: Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services accounted for $91.5M of obligations in FY2026 to date. Research Triangle Institute also sold All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services for $68.6M and Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities for $27.4M. Other notable markets include Other Accounting Services at $19.5M and Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services at $12.2M.

faq.q: How much does Research Triangle Institute make from federal contracts?
faq.a: Research Triangle Institute made $250M in federal contract obligations in FY2026 to date. Research Triangle Institute received those obligations across 289 awards, with an average award size of $866K, and obligations were down 30.8% year over year.

faq.q: Which agencies buy from Research Triangle Institute?
faq.a: The Department of Health and Human Services is the largest buyer, with $194M in FY2026 to date obligations. Other agencies buying from Research Triangle Institute in FY2026 to date include the Environmental Protection Agency ($15.7M), the Department of Labor ($12.9M), the Agency for International Development ($12.3M), and the Department of Education ($8.4M).

faq.q: What does Research Triangle Institute sell to the government?
faq.a: Research Triangle Institute sells management and professional services, research, and technical services to the government. Major markets in FY2026 to date are Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services ($91.5M), All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services ($68.6M), and Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities ($27.4M), plus Other Accounting Services ($19.5M) and Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services ($12.2M).

faq.q: Which Research Triangle Institute contracts are expiring soon?
faq.a: Specific expiring contracts are not listed in the provided materials, so expiring-contract values and award details are not available here. The available figures cover obligations by fiscal year, top buying agencies, and top NAICS markets for FY2026 to date.
